model: Reads the game's memory: where Link is, the room's tiles, objects, health, items. No pixels, no labels written for one game.
Builds its own map while playing: which kinds of ground are walls or doors (learned by walking into them), which exits lead where.
Picks the next goal by value: new things to try in this room first, then the nearest known exit never taken (it travels there over its own map).
Doors: it never re-tries the doorway it just came through as 'new ground', and it steps through gaps that sit between two tiles (read from the game's finer tiles).
Areas: when it looks for unexplored exits, the area it found last comes first, so it goes back into a dungeon instead of drifting across the overworld.
When nothing new has happened for a while: a short burst of random play, then it forgets the walls and failed goals it believed in, and plans again.
Fights only when it picks 'hit that enemy' as a goal (low priority). The trained combat reflex exists but is not switched on in Zelda 1 yet: being tested.
One continuous game per run, from the start screen: no save states, no reloads.

defs.v: the first step a game reaches each goal: first item, second item, a dungeon, a key, using a key (key count drops inside a dungeon), dungeon rooms, map or compass, a heart container (every Zelda boss leaves one), a second dungeon, a fourth item, the ending.
median steps to a goal over the 16 games. One step = 8 frames, the same for every idea.
distinct screens, caves and dungeon rooms entered.
health going down while max health stays the same.
health going up without a heart container; 'when low' = it was at half health or less.
the most steps in a row with no new place, item, key or heart container.
rate in the second half of the game divided by the first half.

limits: 16 games per idea is small: single games range from about 10 to 70 places. That is why the marks use paired intervals.
These are the games I tune on (seeds 8-23). A winner must also win on 16 held-out games before it becomes the default.
Zelda 1 keeps no kill counter, so combat KPIs are blank for it.
'Heart container' stands for beating a boss. Zelda 1 also has a few on the overworld.
The learning ratio drops when the agent gets stuck late in the game (stuck = no fights). Read it next to the longest stall.
